From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Caveat up front:** I have only the Seller's *summary* of its SPA positions and its Disclosure Letter, not the SPA text or the DD-002 to DD-012 documents themselves. Everything below should be verified against the actual drafting and the underlying data room material before it goes into a mark-up. Several of the Seller's characterisations (e.g. "not expected to be material", "ordinary-course", "considered adequate") are advocacy, not facts, and the Disclosure Letter's own item 11 confirms the Seller is not standing behind any conclusion.

---

## A. Overall assessment

The package is not "fair and balanced". It has a consistent architecture that works against the Buyer in three layers:

1. **Collapse every protection into one regime** – fundamental, title, tax and IP warranties are all pushed under the 20% cap / 18-month / basket regime, and the limitations are stated to apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 12.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
2. **Then disclose against all of it** – general disclosure of the entire data room plus public registers (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2), reinforced by a constructive-knowledge bar (cl. 8.3: "discoverable from the data room or public records").
3. **Then leave the known, quantified problems unresolved at Completion** – Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) released "following" Completion, Bluefen consent with no delivery mechanism or conditions evidence, Ironquay SOW3 (AUD 180k) unpaid and unassigned, AUD 420k bonuses left out of the funds flow, a live privacy incident, and AUD 330k of supplier commitments.

The combined effect: the Buyer would pay AUD 24m on a debt-free basis, inherit up to ~AUD 4m of known cash items and consent risk on 30% of revenue, and be told the matters were disclosed/discoverable so no claim lies. Each layer needs to be unpicked.

---

## B. Material issues and reasoning

### 1. Fundamental and title warranties swept into the general cap and time limit — **reject**

The Seller proposes capacity and title warranties be subject to the 20% cap and 18 months "for administrative simplicity". If title to the shares fails, the Buyer's loss is the entire AUD 24m, not AUD 4.8m. There is no administrative burden in carving these out; this is a pure risk transfer.

**Position:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances over shares, share capital) capped at 100% of the price, claim period of 6–7 years (or the statutory limitation period), not subject to de minimis/basket, and not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.

### 2. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" — **reject**

- **Tax:** 18 months is shorter than the ATO's amendment periods. Tax exposure should sit under a separate, first-dollar **tax indemnity** (no de minimis, no basket), capped at 100% of price (or at least a materially higher cap than general), with a 7-year claim period, and not qualified by data-room disclosure.
- **IP:** For an analytics business, IP is the core asset, and the Seller's own disclosure (item 4) shows an unresolved ownership gap on SOW3. IP warranties should have a longer period (3 years minimum) and a higher cap, and the Ironquay matter should be a specific indemnity (see item 9).

### 3. Clause 12.3: "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" — **reject and reverse**

This is a default-flip. The Buyer's standard position is the opposite: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, and expressly **do not** apply to fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity, specific indemnities, leakage/price adjustment claims, breaches of pre-Completion covenants or Completion obligations, fraud, or wilful concealment. If this sentence survives, every carve-out we negotiate elsewhere is at risk of being read back under the cap.

### 4. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for "all Claims of any nature" — **narrow substantially**

- **Fraud / wilful misconduct:** Must be carved out of all limitations and the exclusive-remedy clause. A clause purporting to exclude liability for fraud is likely unenforceable anyway, but we should not leave it to argument.
- **Misleading or deceptive conduct (ACL s 18):** Non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses cannot contract out of s 18. We should refuse any drafting that purports to, and in any event limit the non-reliance acknowledgment to matters outside the SPA, Disclosure Letter and defined Transaction Documents.
- **Specific indemnities and Completion obligations:** Exclusive-remedy must not bar enforcement of the indemnities, price adjustment, or specific performance of Completion deliverables (e.g. delivery of the Riverlark release).
- **Equitable remedies:** Preserve injunctive relief and specific performance for the restraint/confidentiality covenants.

### 5. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2) — **restrict**

The Seller wants everything in the data room (and anything on a public register) to qualify every warranty. Combined with cl. 8.3, this would mean a warranty breach buried in a 400-page contract that nobody flagged is "disclosed".

**Position:**
- Disclosure only operates if **fairly disclosed** – i.e. with sufficient detail to enable a reasonably experienced buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. Mere inclusion of a document is not disclosure of every inference that could be drawn from it.
- No general disclosure of public registers or "publicly searchable corporate records". If the Seller wants to rely on an ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia or court search, it attaches the search to the Disclosure Letter.
- Data room to be frozen, indexed, and delivered on two identical USBs with an agreed index annexed. Note the Seller's cut-off is **5.00pm 22 September 2026** — six weeks ago. Any material added since is not disclosed; we should insist nothing is added without our consent and that disclosure is as at the cut-off only.
- Disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity, or any specific indemnity.
- Minor but worth noting: the Disclosure Letter numbers 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 — there is no 1.3. Ask what was removed and confirm nothing is intended to be incorporated by reference.

### 6. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including matters "discoverable" — **delete or confine to actual knowledge**

As drafted, the Buyer loses the right to claim for anything its advisers *could* have found. That is a constructive-knowledge bar which guts the warranties and shifts the Seller's duty to disclose onto our DD team.

**Position:** Delete. Fallback: limited to **actual** knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, of a matter fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and only to the extent they were actually aware it constituted a breach. Never "discoverable", never advisers' knowledge, never public records.

### 7. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3) — **convert to a proper condition precedent with teeth**

Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26. DD-002 contains a change-of-control consent clause (11.2) *with conditions* (11.3), and the Seller confirms (DL item 2) that there is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Reasonable endeavours" and "treat as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" are not adequate:

- "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest standard. Push for "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours", with specific steps and a Buyer right to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- The condition should be satisfied only on delivery of an **unconditional written consent** (or one on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), **plus** evidence that the 11.3 conditions have been met, with **no** amendment to pricing, term or scope and no termination right triggered.
- Condition for the benefit of the **Buyer only**, waivable only by the Buyer; long-stop date with Buyer termination right.
- Given the concentration, consider a commercial backstop: a portion of the price deferred/escrowed and released on confirmation that Bluefen has not terminated within [12] months post-Completion, or a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract attributable to the change of control.

### 8. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7) — **must be discharged at Completion, not after**

The deal is debt-free/cash-free. The Seller proposes to leave a ~AUD 3.2m secured facility in place at Completion with a release to follow. That is inconsistent with the price basis and leaves the Buyer owning a company that is in default (DD-003 change-of-control 8.1 will trip on Completion) with security still registered.

**Position:**
- Facility repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price** via the funds flow (direct payment to Riverlark), with the repayment amount deducted as Debt in the price mechanics.
- Completion deliverables: executed payoff letter, deed of release and discharge, PPSR financing statement discharge (or signed release forms), release of any guarantee by the Company or any security over the shares. Verify whether Riverlark holds security over the **shares** — if so, this is also a title point (item 15).
- No Completion without these. The Seller's "following Completion" wording should be deleted.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1) — **existing indemnity is inadequate**

DD-004 cl. 7.3 says SOW3 Project Materials transfer **only** on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment. On the documents, the Company does not currently own the SOW3 deliverables. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" would, at best, reimburse the AUD 180k — it does nothing for the loss if Ironquay refuses to assign, licenses the IP to a competitor, or if products built on SOW3 must be withdrawn.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion: Seller procures payment in full and delivers a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay (with moral rights consents from the relevant developers) as a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the Company not holding good title to any Ironquay deliverables (SOW1–3), outside the cap/basket/time limits.
- IP warranty that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business, not qualified by general disclosure of DD-004/DD-010.
- If the AUD 180k is paid pre-Completion by the Company, treat it as a Seller cost (leakage/Debt) rather than a reduction in cash.

### 10. Employee Completion bonuses — AUD 420,000 (DD-005) — **price them in, with on-costs**

The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" yet excludes them from the funds flow. Post-Completion the Company (then owned by us) is the employer and will pay them. On-costs are not addressed: superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025 if the bonuses are OTE), NSW payroll tax (5.45%), and any PAYG/leave accrual interaction. Realistic gross cost is closer to **AUD 490–500k**.

**Position:** Either (a) Seller pays through the Company pre-Completion and it is treated as Debt/transaction expense in the price adjustment, grossed up for on-costs, or (b) deducted from the price and itemised in the funds flow with Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Also confirm who bears the retention element — if bonuses are conditional on continued employment post-Completion, we need to understand whether the Seller expects us to fund retention for its benefit. Add a transaction-bonus warranty and indemnity.

### 11. DD-006 export/privacy incident — **this is not a "preliminary operational matter"**

A download link containing ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps was sent to an unintended external address. That is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the Company has 30 days to assess whether there is likely serious harm, and must notify the OAIC and affected individuals if so. Civil penalties for serious interferences with privacy are now very substantial. The Seller's framing ("not expected to be material", "no loss amount") is not supported by its own disclosure, which concedes the investigation is preliminary and it cannot say whether the file was accessed or whether notification is required.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller completes the NDB assessment (with external privacy counsel), documents it, notifies if required, and provides the Buyer with the report and all correspondence before Completion. Buyer to be consulted on notification decisions.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, third-party claims, customer contract consequences — check whether Bluefen or others have breach-notification or termination rights), outside cap/basket/time limits (or under a separate cap).
- Privacy and data-security warranties not qualified by DD-006 being in the data room.
- Ensure cl. 4.6 / Sch 6 is not drafted so that the "Incident" is a defined, disclosed matter that excludes the Buyer's rights.

### 12. Office lease (DD-007) — **low risk, but close it out**

Seller says it is a notification obligation, not a consent. Verify the lease ourselves. Either way, require the notice be given pre-Completion and evidence delivered, with a warranty that no landlord consent is required and no breach arises from the change of control.

### 13. Supplier renewals — 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011) — **investigate the structure**

Three related renewals of identical amounts, which the Seller itself says must be "read together for timing/scope", is a pattern worth probing: it may reflect a single AUD 330k commitment split into tranches that each sit under a conduct-of-business consent threshold. The Seller declines to say whether they are terminable, accrued, or in the ordinary course.

**Position:** Request the contracts and board/approval record. Confirm whether any was entered into after the locked-box date / outside ordinary course — if so, it is leakage or requires Buyer consent. Any amounts accrued but unpaid at Completion should be in Debt/working capital. Add a conduct-of-business covenant with an aggregate (not per-contract) threshold for new commitments, e.g. AUD 100k individually or AUD 250k in aggregate with related counterparties.

### 14. Mossvale (DD-009) — **verify, do not accept the Seller's reading**

An assignment restriction generally is not triggered by a share sale. But we should read DD-009 ourselves for change-of-control, "control" or "affiliate" language, and obtain a warranty listing *all* contracts with change-of-control or termination-on-sale rights, with Bluefen and Mossvale specifically addressed.

### 15. Title (DD-012) — **a share register is not title verification**

The Seller discloses only that the register shows Harbourglass as 100% holder and expressly says we have not verified. We need to do that verification now:
- ASIC company extract and current constitution (pre-emptive rights, director consent to transfer, any share class differences).
- Share certificates and any options, convertible notes, SAFE instruments, employee equity, or shareholder agreements.
- **PPSR search against Harbourglass and the Company** — if Riverlark (or anyone) has security over the shares, a release is a Completion deliverable.
- Confirm no trust holding or nominee arrangement over the shares.
Title warranties as per item 1: uncapped, long-dated, no disclosure qualification.

### 16. General limitation parameters (cl. 12.1 / 12.2 / 12.3) — **negotiable, but adjust**

- **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m):** Within market range for an Australian private deal, but on the low side given 30% revenue concentration, open IP, and a live privacy incident. Push to 30–50%; alternatively hold at 20% for general warranties **only if** tax, title, IP and the specific indemnities are carved out and sit under higher/no caps. Consider W&I insurance if the Seller will not move.
- **De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k:** Roughly 0.1% / 1% of price — market. But push for a **tipping** basket (recover from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed) rather than excess-only, and ensure the de minimis aggregates related claims.
- **18 months:** Push to 24 months so the Buyer has two audit cycles. Also check what the SPA says about the period for *commencing proceedings* after notice — Sellers often pair a long notice period with a short (3–6 month) sunset to issue; we want 9–12 months and a tolling provision where the claim depends on a third-party claim.

### 17. Price mechanics and funds flow — **the summary is not enough**

"Debt-free/cash-free" has been asserted but the Seller's own package leaves AUD 3.2m of debt, AUD ~0.5m of bonuses, AUD 180k Ironquay and AUD 330k of supplier commitments outside the funds flow. We need the actual mechanism (completion accounts vs locked box), the definitions of Debt, Cash, Transaction Costs and Leakage, and to ensure each item above falls expressly within them. The funds flow should itemise every deduction and third-party payment at Completion.

---

## C. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommended Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties under general cap and 18 months | Reject. 100% of price cap, 6–7 years, no basket, no disclosure qualification. |
| 2 | Tax and IP under general regime | Separate tax indemnity (first dollar, 100% cap, 7 years). IP warranties ≥3 years, higher cap. |
| 3 | Limitations apply to "all Claims unless stated" | Reverse: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims; express carve-outs for fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, fraud. |
| 4 | Exclusive remedy / non-reliance for all Claims | Carve out fraud, ACL s 18, specific indemnities, Completion obligations, equitable relief. |
| 5 | General disclosure of data room and public registers | "Fairly disclosed" standard; no public-register disclosure; frozen indexed data room as at 22 Sept 2026; no disclosure against fundamental/tax/indemnities. Ask about missing para 1.3. |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge incl. "discoverable" matters | Delete. Fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals only. |
| 7 | Bluefen consent (30% revenue) | True Buyer-only CP: unconditional written consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, no adverse terms, all-reasonable-endeavours, long-stop. Consider escrow/deferred consideration or specific indemnity. |
| 8 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m released "following" Completion | Repay at Completion from price; payoff letter, deed of release, PPSR discharge and share-security release as Completion deliverables. |
| 9 | Ironquay SOW3 (AUD 180k unpaid, no assignment) | Payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; uncapped specific indemnity for loss of IP title; unqualified IP warranty. |
| 10 | AUD 420k bonuses outside funds flow | Treat as Debt/transaction cost grossed up for super and payroll tax (~AUD 490–500k); itemise; Seller indemnity. |
| 11 | DD-006 privacy incident | Pre-Completion NDB assessment and notification covenant; uncapped specific indemnity; unqualified privacy warranties; check customer-contract breach-notice triggers. |
| 12 | Office lease notification | Give notice pre-Completion, deliver evidence, warranty no consent needed. |
| 13 | 3 × AUD 110k supplier renewals | Obtain contracts; test against ordinary-course/leakage; aggregate consent threshold in conduct covenant; accrued amounts into Debt/WC. |
| 14 | Mossvale assignment clause | Verify ourselves; warranty listing all change-of-control contracts. |
| 15 | Title evidenced by register only | Complete our own verification (ASIC, constitution, PPSR, certificates, options); uncapped title warranty. |
| 16 | 20% cap / AUD 25k–250k thresholds / 18 months | Push cap to 30–50% (or W&I); tipping basket; 24 months; adequate period to commence proceedings. |
| 17 | Funds flow / price mechanics | Obtain full mechanism; ensure all items above sit within Debt/Transaction Costs/Leakage definitions and are itemised. |

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (i) Riverlark at Completion and funds flow; (ii) Bluefen CP; (iii) carve-outs from the limitation regime (items 1–4); (iv) disclosure/knowledge standard (items 5–6); (v) specific indemnities for Ironquay, DD-006 and bonuses; then the parameter negotiation on cap/basket/time.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for the Seller once we have the SPA text and the underlying DD documents.

- Disclosure only operates if **fairly disclosed** – i.e. with sufficient detail to enable a reasonably experienced buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. Mere inclusion of a document is not disclosure of every inference that could be drawn from it.
- No general disclosure of public registers or "publicly searchable corporate records". If the Seller wants to rely on an ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia or court search, it attaches the search to the Disclosure Letter.
- Data room to be frozen, indexed, and delivered on two identical USBs with an agreed index annexed. Note the Seller's cut-off is **5.00pm 22 September 2026** — six weeks ago. Any material added since is not disclosed; we should insist nothing is added without our consent and that disclosure is as at the cut-off only.
- Disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity, or any specific indemnity.
- Minor but worth noting: the Disclosure Letter numbers 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 — there is no 1.3. Ask what was removed and confirm nothing is intended to be incorporated by reference.

### 6. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including matters "discoverable" — **delete or confine to actual knowledge**

As drafted, the Buyer loses the right to claim for anything its advisers *could* have found. That is a constructive-knowledge bar which guts the warranties and shifts the Seller's duty to disclose onto our DD team.

**Position:** Delete. Fallback: limited to **actual** knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, of a matter fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and only to the extent they were actually aware it constituted a breach. Never "discoverable", never advisers' knowledge, never public records.

### 7. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3) — **convert to a proper condition precedent with teeth**

Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26. DD-002 contains a change-of-control consent clause (11.2) *with conditions* (11.3), and the Seller confirms (DL item 2) that there is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Reasonable endeavours" and "treat as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" are not adequate:

- "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest standard. Push for "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours", with specific steps and a Buyer right to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- The condition should be satisfied only on delivery of an **unconditional written consent** (or one on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), **plus** evidence that the 11.3 conditions have been met, with **no** amendment to pricing, term or scope and no termination right triggered.
- Condition for the benefit of the **Buyer only**, waivable only by the Buyer; long-stop date with Buyer termination right.
- Given the concentration, consider a commercial backstop: a portion of the price deferred/escrowed and released on confirmation that Bluefen has not terminated within [12] months post-Completion, or a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract attributable to the change of control.

### 8. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7) — **must be discharged at Completion, not after**

The deal is debt-free/cash-free. The Seller proposes to leave a ~AUD 3.2m secured facility in place at Completion with a release to follow. That is inconsistent with the price basis and leaves the Buyer owning a company that is in default (DD-003 change-of-control 8.1 will trip on Completion) with security still registered.

**Position:**
- Facility repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price** via the funds flow (direct payment to Riverlark), with the repayment amount deducted as Debt in the price mechanics.
- Completion deliverables: executed payoff letter, deed of release and discharge, PPSR financing statement discharge (or signed release forms), release of any guarantee by the Company or any security over the shares. Verify whether Riverlark holds security over the **shares** — if so, this is also a title point (item 15).
- No Completion without these. The Seller's "following Completion" wording should be deleted.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1) — **existing indemnity is inadequate**

DD-004 cl. 7.3 says SOW3 Project Materials transfer **only** on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment. On the documents, the Company does not currently own the SOW3 deliverables. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" would, at best, reimburse the AUD 180k — it does nothing for the loss if Ironquay refuses to assign, licenses the IP to a competitor, or if products built on SOW3 must be withdrawn.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion: Seller procures payment in full and delivers a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay (with moral rights consents from the relevant developers) as a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the Company not holding good title to any Ironquay deliverables (SOW1–3), outside the cap/basket/time limits.
- IP warranty that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business, not qualified by general disclosure of DD-004/DD-010.
- If the AUD 180k is paid pre-Completion by the Company, treat it as a Seller cost (leakage/Debt) rather than a reduction in cash.

### 10. Employee Completion bonuses — AUD 420,000 (DD-005) — **price them in, with on-costs**

The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" yet excludes them from the funds flow. Post-Completion the Company (then owned by us) is the employer and will pay them. On-costs are not addressed: superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025 if the bonuses are OTE), NSW payroll tax (5.45%), and any PAYG/leave accrual interaction. Realistic gross cost is closer to **AUD 490–500k**.

**Position:** Either (a) Seller pays through the Company pre-Completion and it is treated as Debt/transaction expense in the price adjustment, grossed up for on-costs, or (b) deducted from the price and itemised in the funds flow with Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Also confirm who bears the retention element — if bonuses are conditional on continued employment post-Completion, we need to understand whether the Seller expects us to fund retention for its benefit. Add a transaction-bonus warranty and indemnity.

### 11. DD-006 export/privacy incident — **this is not a "preliminary operational matter"**

A download link containing ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps was sent to an unintended external address. That is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the Company has 30 days to assess whether there is likely serious harm, and must notify the OAIC and affected individuals if so. Civil penalties for serious interferences with privacy are now very substantial. The Seller's framing ("not expected to be material", "no loss amount") is not supported by its own disclosure, which concedes the investigation is preliminary and it cannot say whether the file was accessed or whether notification is required.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller completes the NDB assessment (with external privacy counsel), documents it, notifies if required, and provides the Buyer with the report and all correspondence before Completion. Buyer to be consulted on notification decisions.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, third-party claims, customer contract consequences — check whether Bluefen or others have breach-notification or termination rights), outside cap/basket/time limits (or under a separate cap).
- Privacy and data-security warranties not qualified by DD-006 being in the data room.
- Ensure cl. 4.6 / Sch 6 is not drafted so that the "Incident" is a defined, disclosed matter that excludes the Buyer's rights.

### 12. Office lease (DD-007) — **low risk, but close it out**

Seller says it is a notification obligation, not a consent. Verify the lease ourselves. Either way, require the notice be given pre-Completion and evidence delivered, with a warranty that no landlord consent is required and no breach arises from the change of control.

### 13. Supplier renewals — 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011) — **investigate the structure**

Three related renewals of identical amounts, which the Seller itself says must be "read together for timing/scope", is a pattern worth probing: it may reflect a single AUD 330k commitment split into tranches that each sit under a conduct-of-business consent threshold. The Seller declines to say whether they are terminable, accrued, or in the ordinary course.

**Position:** Request the contracts and board/approval record. Confirm whether any was entered into after the locked-box date / outside ordinary course — if so, it is leakage or requires Buyer consent. Any amounts accrued but unpaid at Completion should be in Debt/working capital. Add a conduct-of-business covenant with an aggregate (not per-contract) threshold for new commitments, e.g. AUD 100k individually or AUD 250k in aggregate with related counterparties.

### 14. Mossvale (DD-009) — **verify, do not accept the Seller's reading**

An assignment restriction generally is not triggered by a share sale. But we should read DD-009 ourselves for change-of-control, "control" or "affiliate" language, and obtain a warranty listing *all* contracts with change-of-control or termination-on-sale rights, with Bluefen and Mossvale specifically addressed.

### 15. Title (DD-012) — **a share register is not title verification**

The Seller discloses only that the register shows Harbourglass as 100% holder and expressly says we have not verified. We need to do that verification now:
- ASIC company extract and current constitution (pre-emptive rights, director consent to transfer, any share class differences).
- Share certificates and any options, convertible notes, SAFE instruments, employee equity, or shareholder agreements.
- **PPSR search against Harbourglass and the Company** — if Riverlark (or anyone) has security over the shares, a release is a Completion deliverable.
- Confirm no trust holding or nominee arrangement over the shares.
Title warranties as per item 1: uncapped, long-dated, no disclosure qualification.

### 16. General limitation parameters (cl. 12.1 / 12.2 / 12.3) — **negotiable, but adjust**

- **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m):** Within market range for an Australian private deal, but on the low side given 30% revenue concentration, open IP, and a live privacy incident. Push to 30–50%; alternatively hold at 20% for general warranties **only if** tax, title, IP and the specific indemnities are carved out and sit under higher/no caps. Consider W&I insurance if the Seller will not move.
- **De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k:** Roughly 0.1% / 1% of price — market. But push for a **tipping** basket (recover from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed) rather than excess-only, and ensure the de minimis aggregates related claims.
- **18 months:** Push to 24 months so the Buyer has two audit cycles. Also check what the SPA says about the period for *commencing proceedings* after notice — Sellers often pair a long notice period with a short (3–6 month) sunset to issue; we want 9–12 months and a tolling provision where the claim depends on a third-party claim.

### 17. Price mechanics and funds flow — **the summary is not enough**

"Debt-free/cash-free" has been asserted but the Seller's own package leaves AUD 3.2m of debt, AUD ~0.5m of bonuses, AUD 180k Ironquay and AUD 330k of supplier commitments outside the funds flow. We need the actual mechanism (completion accounts vs locked box), the definitions of Debt, Cash, Transaction Costs and Leakage, and to ensure each item above falls expressly within them. The funds flow should itemise every deduction and third-party payment at Completion.
